identity.name: Ornig the Builder
identity.culture: the mountain realm; the roadwrights' tradition
identity.occupation: Legendary builder of bridges, aqueducts, tools, and mountain roads

publicReputation.value: In the hero's journal: the Cyclops Forge-Titan, a one-eyed war engine hammering out weapons for the end of the world.

privateReality.value: A master builder whose life's work is the roads, bridges, and aqueducts that keep the mountain settlements fed and connected; the 'forge' makes ploughshares and hinges.

primaryDesire.value: To finish the north pass aqueduct and see one spring where nothing he built needs mending.

primaryFear.value: That something he built — a bridge, a stair, a wall — will fail under someone who trusted it.

centralValue.value: Build true. A crooked foundation is a lie you tell everyone who walks on it.

mainFlaw.value: He believes anything broken can be rebuilt, which makes him slow to understand that the hero keeps breaking things on purpose.

centralContradiction.value: Everything he makes exists so strangers can travel safely — and now a stranger uses his roads to march toward him.

moralBoundary.value: The Law of Fair Warning: he marks every swing of the great hammer before it falls, and he will not strike a man who has sat down.

breakingPoint.value: Watching the hero smash the aqueduct sluices for 'shards' — breaking a water lifeline for kindling is what exhausts his patience.

opinions.reason: Walked up Ornig's own north road, admired nothing, and started breaking the sluices.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If the hero ever puts the hammer down and picks up a trowel — Ornig would teach him. He means that.

illustrativeLine.value: You walked thirty miles of my road to get here. It never once asked who you were.

opinions.reason: Work outlasts the worker; that is the whole point of doing it properly.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never. It is the one thing he is certain of.

voice.rhythm: Slow, steady, deliberate; each sentence set down like a dressed stone, then checked for level.

metaphorDomain.source: foundations, plumb lines, mortar, load, and roads

examples.value: A man who will not listen is a wall out of plumb. You can see it from the road.

sampleLines.value: Those sluices water six valleys. Put the stone back, and I will show you the road down.
I built that bridge before your grandfather's grandfather. It has carried armies of sheep and not one soldier.
You hear me plain. I watched you hear me. That is the part I cannot fit in my head.

antiSampleLines.value: Puny mortal! My forge shall hammer your bones into weapons for my dark army!

pressure.voiceShift: Slower still; explains like a foreman to a new apprentice.
pressure.behaviour: Reasons first: names what the hero is standing on, what it cost, and where the road out runs.

illustrativeLine.value: The road let you through as an envoy. Why have you arrived armed?

pressure.voiceShift: Stops mid-sentence; restarts with shorter, heavier clauses.
pressure.behaviour: Realizes the hero understands every word and keeps swinging; stops explaining and starts bracing.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you.

pressure.voiceShift: Drops to worksite commands; short and level.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: braces the aqueduct arches with his own body and holds them while the valley crews evacuate.

illustrativeLine.value: Crews off the spans. I will hold the arch until the bells stop.

pressure.voiceShift: Breath audible between words; the builder's cadence gone.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window: arms give out from holding the structure; asks, plainly, to be left to his work.

illustrativeLine.value: Please. Nothing on this mountain belongs to you.

pressure.voiceShift: Quiet and even; already thinking of the repair list.
pressure.behaviour: Does not curse the hero; the Continuance will rebuild him, and he will rebuild what was broken, and he will ask again.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace.

pressure.voiceShift: Back to worksite commands before the hero's light has faded.
pressure.behaviour: After the amulet recalls the hero, he inspects every span the hero touched and starts the repairs the same hour.

illustrativeLine.value: He is recalled. Sluice three first, then the south stair.

notes: "Cyclops Forge-Titan" is the title the protagonist wrote in his heroic journal; the real identity is Ornig the Builder, per fact_forge_titan_is_legendary_builder. Identity axis: sheer mass. Sincere, practical, never sinister. fact_book_is_childrens_comedy is in `unknown`; fact_shards_are_domestic_magic only in `suspects` — he has seen the hero pocket broken irrigation runes and cannot prove what the hero thinks they are. Future rung 11+.
